To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate electrically controlled modulation (increase or decrease) of visible spontaneous emission from colloidal quantum dots via the dynamic control of local density of states.
we have electrically controlled the local density of the optical states around quantum dots in a gated plasmoelectrochemical heterostructure.

1) the local density of photonic states in the vicinity of a single colloidal quantum dot is dynamically controlled by electrically modulating the optical permittivity of an ultrathim TiN film in a gated TiNSiO2Ag heterostructure; 2) the dynamic control of the local density states leads to the modulation of spontaneous emission rate, radiative efficiency, and far-field emission intensity of colloidal quantum dot.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new optical and electrical methods for the dynamic control of the emission intensity from colloidal quantum dots.
the development of a new type of optoelectronic devices based on the electric field control of the local density states around a quantum dots.
the development of new approaches for the electrical modulation of light emission properties from colloidal quantum dots.

the authors demonstrate the electrically controlled manipulation of the local density states in a plasmonic heterostucture, which results in the modulation of spontaneous emission rate, emission intensity, and emission quantum yield of colloidal quantum dot.

this work provides an electrically controlled modulation mechanism for the intensity of visible light from colloidal quantum dots, and it may have a significant impact in display and lighting technologies.
we have demonstrated electrically controlled emission of colloidal quantum dot in a plasmonic heterostucture.

the local density of state (LDOS) around a single quantum dot (SQD) is electrically controllable via field-effect modulation of the optical permittivity of an ultrathins TiN film incorporated in a TiN/Si02/Ag plasmon heterostructure.
we demonstrate the electrically controlled dynamic control of light intensity from a colloidal quantum dot in the visible spectral range.

we have developed an electrical control scheme for the modulation of the local photonic density of states in the vicinity of a colloidal quantum dot, which results in the modulation of its spontaneous emission rate and emission intensity.

it provides a new approach to modulate the intensity of visible light from quantum dots.
we can dynamically control the spontaneous emission rate and far-field emission intensity of colloidal QD at constant optical pumping.
